post.caption: Glenn Miller's gold record was spray paint. By February 1942 his song Chattanooga Choo Choo had sold 1.2 million copies. His label, RCA Victor, answered with the first gold record, presented during a live radio broadcast. The announcer, Paul Douglas, called it solid gold on the air. It was only a copy of the record, sprayed with gold paint. The label did it as a publicity stunt, not an award. The song came from the 1941 film Sun Valley Serenade. The Recording Industry Association of America started official gold certification in 1958, and the first official gold single was Perry Como's Catch a Falling Star.
